section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace" and the emphasis on peace in the redemption.
section.t: "He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me, for many were with me"1,
and it is known what was written2
by the Alter Rebbe to the gaon and chassid R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev3,
"When I read... 'He redeemed my soul in peace'... I emerged in peace from Havayah of peace."
And from this it is understood that the matter of peace in the redemption is a primary matter,
therefore he emphasizes this matter
(three times4)
in his letter: "redeemed in peace,"
"I emerged in peace,"
"from Havayah of peace."
And so it is also understood from the Igeres HaKodesh in Tanya, end of section 2, which was written after his return from Petersburg
(to all Anash)
whose conclusion and seal is that there should be peace etc.,
the conduct in a manner that "Hashem will place in the heart of their brothers, as water reflects a face etc."
And it is also evident from this that in many Chassidic discourses on this verse5,
and especially in the discourses of 19 Kislev,
it is explained that the matter and novelty of this redemption is that the redemption is in peace.
And it needs to be understood,
for seemingly the main thing is the essence of the matter of redemption
(whether regarding Dovid, the sweet singer of Israel
(and also regarding Dovid, King Moshiach6),
and whether regarding the Alter Rebbe, the master of joy and redemption,
the main matter is that he went from imprisonment to freedom),
and what is the emphasis specifically of "in peace"?
And furthermore, it needs to be understood,
the continuation of "He redeemed my soul in peace" is as stated in the verse "from the battle that was against me, for many were with me,"
and since the redemption is "from the battle," meaning war,
and also that there are many
(except that on the contrary, "the many were with me" – as stated in the Yerushalmi7),
it is understood that the redemption in itself would have had to be in a manner of war.
And if so, it needs to be understood what is the necessity that the redemption specifically be in peace.
And the point of the matter,
is explained in the discourse "Padeh BeShalom" of the Mitteler Rebbe,
the successor of the master of joy and redemption
(in Shaarei Teshuvah – Shaar HaTefillah),
that when the service is from the aspect of Yechidah,
then the redemption is in peace.
